thread:
eli: Heads-up — I ran a quick dry-run of the autoscaler drain on the gpu-pool in us-west2 and hit a failure case where a long-running preemptible training job blocked scale-down.

sasha: Ah, which failure? PDB rejection or actual pod eviction timeout?

eli: PDB + node has local-ssd attached, so kubelet refused to evict some pods (they were using hostPath for checkpoint). Drain got stuck at 'eviction API denied by PDB' for two pods.

jamie: Oof. Were those pods using best-effort or a PriorityClass?

eli: priorityClass=bulk-training (value 500). Not critical but not lowest. No preemptionPolicy set, so they were preemptible by default.

katie: Could we add a temporary annotation that allows autoscaler to override PDBs for scale-down in non-prod? We talked about a 'drain-override' label last quarter.

eli: I tried that: annotated node with cluster.autoscaler/force-eviction=true and ran the drain manager, but eviction API still respects PDBs unless the controller-patch is applied.

devin: Two options: 1) adjust PDB minAvailable for those pods, or 2) use PriorityClass with preemptionPolicy=Never? Neither ideal.

jamie: We should avoid preemptionPolicy=Never for long jobs. It breaks autoscaler flexibility. What about a small cf: Add a new PriorityClass tier 'gpu-ephemeral' with lower priority than bulk-training and a small TTL on checkpoints so they can be recreated on restart.

eli: Proposed short-term mitigation that worked in dry-run: cordon node, copy local-ssd checkpoints to GCS via rsync in a k8s Job, then drain. But that's hacky and slow (~6-8m).

sasha: For long-term: I'd like a documented golden path for safe evictions: 1) Pod owners opt into a CSI snapshot or checkpoint sidecar for local state. 2) Use PDB minAvailable=0 for non-critical workers. 3) Cluster autoscaler uses annotation cluster.autoscaler/allow-pdb-override on scale events in preconfigured grace windows.

eli: Agree. Also propose autoscaler change: when scale-down candidate node is gpu-type, consult 'gpu-eviction-policy' ConfigMap in kube-system (policy: snapshot-first|force-after-Ns|skip) and act accordingly.

devin: Can we prototype a controller that: on Node.ScaleDownCandidate -> labels pods with 'eviction-phase=prepare', triggers snapshot sidecar, waits up to X, then proceeds to eviction and only uses PDB override if snapshot succeeded?

jamie: That controller would reduce failures and keep PDB semantics for owners who opted in. Also helps cost: we avoid prolonging preemptible nodes unnecessarily.

katie: Cost note: every failed drain on a p-spot GPU node delays scale-down 30m avg, that's ~0.5 GPU-hours wasted. At 3$/GPU-hour that's small per node but scales to $$$ across fleet. We should quantify this in the RFC.

eli: I'll open a brief RFC with example controller design + kubectl snippets and an integration test plan. Draft sketch:

```
# sample commands for dry-run
kubectl cordon node/gpu-abcdef
kubectl annotate node/gpu-abcdef cluster.autoscaler/scale-down-candidate=true
# simulate snapshot sidecar
kubectl run snapshot-job --image=redwood/devops-tools:latest -- /bin/sh -c "tar -czf /tmp/ckpt.tgz /var/checkpoints && gsutil cp /tmp/ckpt.tgz gs://redwood-checkpoints/$NODE/"
kubectl drain node/gpu-abcdef --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=300 --timeout=15m
```

sasha: Add an alternative: a 'soft-drain' flow where the node is cordoned and traffic is stopped, but pods stay for N minutes to allow owner migration, with a Slack DM to owners. That reduces forced evictions during business hours.

eli: Good idea. We should tie the soft-drain window to region constraints too — us-west2 has stricter capacity on some days.

jamie: Who wants to own the prototype? I'll take the controller PoC; eli do the RFC; sasha handle guardrails and K8s RBAC for allow-pdb-override.

eli: I'll start the RFC now and post link here when ready.

oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: run 'gpu-pool-dry-run' playbook on 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC :robot_face:

katie: :thumbsup: Also add a short checklist for on-call to follow when they see a stuck scale-down in metrics: 1) check PDBs 2) check node local disk usage 3) check pod priorityclass 4) contact owner via DM 5) if allowed, perform snapshot and force drain.

eli: Added checklist to the RFC draft, will ping people once link is up. Thanks everyone.
